title: Swarm coordination runbook and customer notice patterns
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the "swarm" coordination pattern for incidents that require rapid cross-team engagement (multi-service degradations, noisy neighbors, regional capacity events). It includes a short, time-boxed containment checklist, step-by-step coordination flows, role definitions, customer notice and status-page templates, and the post-incident investigation cadence. Use this runbook for incidents that meet the Swarm criteria (see section below).

When to use this runbook
-----------------------
- Use for multi-service or multi-team incidents (3+ teams impacted).
- Use when SLO impact is: availability drop >= 3% or error rate spike (5xx) above 1% for 5+ minutes.
- Use when a regional or capacity constraint causes cascading failures (e.g., GPU farm / routing tier / cache invalidation).

Swarm criteria checklist (quick assessment)
------------------------------------------
1. Impact breadth: are >2 product routes or services degraded? (yes/no)
2. Customer impact: are paid customers experiencing errors or latency above SLA thresholds? (yes/no)
3. Time sensitivity: is the incident actively growing? (yes/no)
If two or more answers are yes, escalate to Swarm.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Incident Lead (IL): owns triage decisions, customer comms cadence, and bridge coordination. Typically Senior SRE on-shift.
- Bridge Operator: runs the conference bridge, collects evidence, updates status.
- Service Leads: owners for each affected service; responsible for containment and short-term mitigations.
- Platform Capacity Lead: evaluates capacity, autoscaling, and hardware pool health.
- Communications Lead: drafts public and customer-specific messages (CS/AE-run).
- Engineering Liaison (per team): implements fixes, rollbacks, or configuration changes.
- Postmortem Author: appointed during incident close; drives RCA timeline.

Immediate containment checklist — first 15 minutes
------------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge and classify (0–2 min)
   - Pager acknowledged in Slack / PagerDuty.
   - IL assigned on the bridge.
   - Short headline: impact, region, estimated customers (post to #incidents).
2. Stabilize (2–10 min)
   - Apply traffic-limiting rules or throttles to noisy routes.
   - Temporarily disable non-essential background jobs or batches.
   - If CPU/GPU saturation suspected: route traffic to alternate pool or enable burst capacity.
3. Evidence capture (2–10 min)
   - Capture SLO dashboards: 1m/5m error rates, p95/p99 latency, request volume.
   - Collect recent deploys, config changes, autoscaler events (last 60 minutes).
   - Snapshot relevant logs and stack traces (link to centralized log view).
4. Customer triage (10–15 min)
   - Communications Lead posts initial status (see templates below).
   - Identify top affected customers and flag AE/CS.

Investigation run loop — 15–90 minutes
-------------------------------------
- Timebox 15-minute investigation sprints with short syncs on the bridge.
- Typical checks (parallel across Service Leads):
  - Dependency health: Redis/memcache hit rates, DB connection pool errors.
  - Model-serving queues: KV cache misses, OOMs on GPU nodes, quantization mismatch errors.
  - Autoscaler: scaling events, cooldowns, throttling logs.
  - Networking: LB error codes, TLS handshake failures, regional routing spikes.
- Use the evidence matrix to mark implicated components. Update the IL every sprint.

Restoration & mitigation steps
------------------------------
1. Priority mitigations (apply in order of least to most impactful):
   - Route around: shift traffic to healthy region or model variant.
   - Config rollbacks: revert the most recent deploys for implicated services.
   - Increase capacity: temporarily add burst nodes or expand GPU pool (with capacity lead).
   - Feature gates: flip off heavy features (large-context generations, long-streaming sessions).
2. Validation: confirm SLO and throttling metrics recovering for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows.
3. Gradual restore: reintroduce features / routes in canary stages, monitor for regressions.

Customer communications patterns and templates
-------------------------------------------
Principles: be timely, transparent, and measurable. Provide next steps and expected updates.

Status snippet templates (short)
- Initial (within 15 min):
  "We are investigating increased error rates for text generation in us-west-2. Customers may see timeouts or 5xx responses. Our engineers are actively triaging and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impacted customers: internal estimate ~8% of requests."
- Update (every 30–60 min):
  "Progress update: root cause narrowed to GPU autoscaler failing to add nodes after burst threshold. We have routed traffic to a healthy region and are seeing partial recovery (errors down from 7% to 2%). Next update in 45 minutes or earlier for major changes."
- Resolution/Close:
  "Resolved: services restored and error rates are back within SLO. We are performing a post-incident review and will publish a summary within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, contact support@redwood.example.com."

Customer-specific template (for high-touch customers)
- Subject: Incident update — service degradation impacting model inference
- Body: "We detected degraded inference performance impacting X% of requests in us-west-2. Our engineering team placed a temporary traffic reroute and reduced batch sizes to limit timeouts. We expect further improvement in the next hour. Your account team (cc'd) will follow up with any mitigation options for your workloads."

Status page examples (markdown-friendly)
| Component | Status | Impact | Next update |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Inference API (us-west-2) | Degraded | 8% of requests | 30m |
| Model-serving pool (g4dn) | Recovering | Partial saturation | 30m |

Postmortem and RCA cadence
--------------------------
- Postmortem timeline (mandatory for Sev 2+ incidents):
  - 0–72 hours: Postmortem draft created. Evidence attached (dashboards, logs, deploys).
  - 72–120 hours: Root cause analysis and action items finalized. Assign owners and due dates.
  - 7 days: Postmortem published and shared with stakeholders; action items entered into the tracking board.
- Postmortem must include: timeline, impact quantification (customers, duration, SLO delta), contributing factors, root cause, mitigation steps, and follow-ups with owners and target dates.
- Required artifacts: Grafana snapshots (png), log archive link, deployment IDs, autoscaler events export.

On-call rotation transition checklist (handover)
---------------------------------------------
1. Before handoff (outgoing):
   - Summarize active incidents and ongoing mitigations in #incidents channel.
   - Ensure bridge notes are up to date with next steps.
   - Notify incoming on-call of any scheduled maintenance or high-risk deployments.
2. Handoff (incoming):
   - Confirm understanding of active mitigations and timers.
   - Verify that SLO dashboards are visible and alert channels are functional.
   - Acknowledge on the rotation calendar.

Game day / simulation exercises (recommended cadence)
----------------------------------------------------
- Quarterly service-swarm drills: simulate noisy neighbor causing capacity saturation and require cross-team coordination.
- Objectives: practice IL assignment, customer comms in 15 minutes, and deploy rollback in 30 minutes.
- Scoring: time-to-first-communication, time-to-stabilize, completeness of post-exercise postmortem.

Appendix A — quick runbook snippets and commands
------------------------------------------------
- Check error rate in Grafana (example query):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="inference-api"}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[1m])) * 100
- Identify recent deploys (CI tagging):
  curl -s "https://ci.redwood.internal/api/v1/deploys?service=inference-api&since=60m" | jq '.'
- Temporarily scale pool: (k8s example)
  kubectl -n inference-scale set --replicas=5 deploy/inference-worker || true

Appendix B — evidence capture checklist
--------------------------------------
- Dashboards: p95/p99 latency, error rate, request volume (1m/5m), autoscaler events.
- Logs: capture last 30 minutes for implicated services.
- Deployments: list of commits and deploy IDs in prior 120 minutes.
- Config changes: feature flags or runtime config updates in prior 120 minutes.

Ownership and escalation path
----------------------------
- Document owner: Evelyn Park (oncall process lead).
- Primary escalation: SRE Manager (Diego Martinez) -> VP Eng (TBD) for Sev 1.
- For legal/compliance-affecting incidents, loop in Security and Legal within first 60 minutes.
